messages:
michael: FYI onboarding hf/chat-x into Redwood Dedicated — function-calling paths are producing invalid JSON for tool args, looks like special tokens are bleeding into the payload
anya: ugh, logs? small repro?
michael: pasted a failing response below — note the extra token markers inside the JSON string:
```
Response: {"name": "get_price", "arguments": "{\"symbol\": \"BTC\", \"start\": \"2023-01-01\"<|json_end|>\"}"}
```
michael: the model inserted its <|json_end|> special token mid-args. downstream JSON parser fails
kai: is that token defined in the HF tokenizer as an additional_special_token? check config.json
michael: yep. snippets from model repo config.json:
```
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<|json_start|>", "<|json_end|>", "<|tool|>"]
}
```
kai: that explains it. Redwood runtime uses JSON-mode boundary markers (e.g., \u0001 markers) and our tool-tagging policy expects to see clean JSON between them. model's special tokens collide with our markers after decode
sam: also saw weirdness when we quantized the model to 4-bit — some token ids moved and the tokenizer->decoder mapping produced an extra spacer token (id 50256) that the HF tokenizer emits as <|tool|> for this model
lucy: can we strip special tokens with tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) before handing to the parser? will that remove legitimate tool tags too?
kai: risky: skip_special_tokens will remove all additional_special_tokens including <|json_end|> so we lose the semantic boundary. better to remap model tokens to non-colliding placeholders at load time, e.g., tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<json_HF_json_start>"]}) then update the prompt/templates to use different tags
anya: but we need backward compatibility with existing prompts that expect <|json_start|>. migrating users will be painful
infra-bot: deploy-note: temporary mitigation deployed to staging — middleware now post-processes outputs and runs a fixed regex to remove known HF special token substrings inside JSON blocks before parse (non-invasive, opt-in via header X-RW-JSON-FIX) :rocket:

michael: infra mitigation upped parse success from 0.63 -> 0.92 on our smoke set. eval-bot results below:
```
Eval run: tool-calling-json-parse
baseline (no fix): 63/100 success
with regex-strip: 92/100 success
with token-remap (local): 98/100 success
```

sam: longer-term we should: 1) add tokenizer collision detection during model onboarding (detect any additional_special_tokens that match our schema), 2) fail onboarding with recommended remap or automatic renaming, 3) add unit tests that run quantized variants and compare decoded special token strings
kai: agree. also add a prompt-template lint that rejects literal collisions like "<|json_start|>" present in both model special tokens and runtime markers
lucy: will open onboarding PR with a checklist and small script: detect collisions, print suggested token map, and optional auto-remap flag
anya: note: some OSS chat templates rely on being able to embed literal tokens (we must offer an escape or canonical mapping)
michael: for now, include a migration note in the release notes and tell customers to set X-RW-JSON-FIX header if they hit parsing errors. will follow up with a proposal for permanent onboarding checks + token remap tool
eval-bot: tagging: regression-suite scheduled for tomorrow with quantized 4-bit + 8-bit combos. I'll post the detailed logs then :mag:
anya: thanks — great catch, and nice quick mitigation :thumbsup:
